questions.question: Which of these is unlawful?

options.text: Pass another vehicle in a marked no passing zone.
Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to cross the center line to pass on hills, in curves, or anywhere you cannot see far enough ahead to pass safely. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, in no passing zones, or where a solid yellow line is next to your lane. Do not pass when the car in front has stopped for a pedestrian or in work zones where passing is dangerous.

questions.question: How can you avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes?

options.text: Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.
Say "No thanks, I'm driving" if someone offers you a drink.

questions.explanation: The only way to avoid drinking and driving risks is to decide before you start drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, making it harder to make safe decisions once you have started drinking.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming conditions that may be hazardous. You may see an upcoming change in traffic direction, a steep downgrade, or another dangerous situation that needs your attention.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers they must slow down. If a new speed limit is shown on this sign, the new speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: When may you drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: As long as you are not driving.
If you are sitting in the back seat.
If you are sitting in the back of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have any open alcoholic beverage while on a public road or sidewalk. You cannot have an open alcohol container in the driver or passenger area of a vehicle on any public road.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on a public highway if no other limit is posted?
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on a public highway is 55 miles per hour. If a different speed limit is posted, follow that posted limit instead.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: On the immediate left side of the cab.
Both on the immediate left side of the cab and directly behind the truck body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both on the immediate left side of the cab and directly behind the truck body.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than smaller cars. The driver cannot see your car behind the truck, and you cannot see traffic ahead if you drive too close behind the truck. If the driver cannot see your car in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: Night driving is challenging because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving creates special challenges for drivers. Because you cannot see as well, it is hard to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are traveling. You can only see as far as your headlights shine.

questions.question: Is it illegal for a vehicle to drive on a sidewalk, except to cross it?
questions.explanation: Drivers crossing a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, alley, or parking lot must yield to pedestrians. It is illegal to drive on a sidewalk except to cross it.

questions.question: When can you change lanes while turning?

options.text: When there are multiple turning lanes.

questions.explanation: When turning, move from one lane to another as directly as possible without crossing lane lines or blocking traffic. You may change lanes only after you have completed your turn.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of a hazard ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
You do not need to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. Stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp right turn ahead.
Right turns are only allowed on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp right turn ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs have a bright yellow-green background. They tell you about road conditions ahead, like curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
How much time passes between drinks

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating can slow alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent you from becoming impaired if you drink too much.

questions.question: What should you do if an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you?

options.text: Speed up to stay away from it.
Stop right away and block its path.
Do everything you can to clear a path for it.
Signal to it when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear a path for it.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, do everything you can to give it a clear path. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road to let it pass.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. You can reduce the risk by driving slower.

questions.question: What problems can worn or bald tires cause?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. They also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Even with mirrors, there are blind spots you cannot see. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check these areas.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: When turning, lower your speed so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to unexpected situations.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs usually look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red colors.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow colors.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black colors.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. You will see them on the right side of the road, or on both sides if the road is divided.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. Always follow the flagger's directions. Flaggers wear bright orange, yellow, or yellow-green clothing. They use paddles and red flags to direct traffic and allow workers to cross safely.

questions.question: If your car's suspension is bad, it can cause:
questions.explanation: Your suspension helps you control your vehicle and gives you a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot after hitting a bump or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: Wearing both your lap belt and shoulder belt increases your protection in an accident.
questions.explanation: Always wear both your lap belt and shoulder belt. Wearing just one part does not protect you as well.

questions.question: To enter a gap in highway traffic:

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check for vehicles around you. Always look to the side and behind your vehicle before you move into another lane.

questions.question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.
questions.explanation: Continuous hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Drive slowly in bad weather to avoid needing hard braking.
